summary:
[  edit  ]
The OP Find  DAT  traverses the component hierarchy starting at one component and looking at all nodes within that component, and outputs a table with one row per node that matches criteria the user chooses. For example, the criteria could be all Ramp TOPs, or all nodes whose name starts with “ wave ”, or all nodes with the  Clone  parameter set to “ master1 ”, or all Geometry components with a tag called “ emitter ”.
The criteria can limited to include only nodes of certain families, or certain operator types. It can filter on matching its path, certain parameters containing certain values (both constant and expressions), comments, tags, or the content of a  DAT  containing certain strings.
You can also cause the  DAT  to only look to some depth of the hierarchy from the specified component, such as 2 levels down, or limitless.
Criteria can be case-sensitive or not, but case-sensitive On or Off applies to all criteria in the OP Find  DAT .
Furthermore you can exclude some nodes using more specialized criteria by returning a True of False in a callback contained in the attached callback  DAT .
With the Combine Filters Menu (Any or All, Default is All), you can do an "or" or "and" on the pattern matching criterea.
It also takes an optional  DAT  containing a list of operators (eg, another OP Find  DAT ) which can be used to chain filters.
Output Columns
There is a variety of columns that you can select from including  name ,  id ,  paths ,  type  and  tags .  ( id  is a member of the operator, which is an integer unique to the node, and doesn't change during the running of the TouchDesigner process.)
You can also output custom columns by defining the column names in the callback  DAT , and filling in the column cells via another function in the callback  DAT . For example, you can output a custom column which is the  tx  parameter value of the node.
You can control when the OP Find  DAT  cooks. Normally it cooks whenever any of the nodes in the specified hierarchy changes. Using the Active  Cook  menu parameter, you can also force-cook it every frame, or turn off cooking entirely.  You can also click the  Pulse  parameter on Active  Cook  in order to force-cook it once, or do the equivalent using the node.cookpulse.pulse() python call.
Instead of being give the path to a component to start at, the OP Find  DAT  can take an input  DAT  containing a pre-generated list of paths to nodes to start from, and merge the results of each input line together in the output. To use this, the input  DAT  should contain the node “id” as the first column, which can be generated with another OP Find  DAT  with the Column called “ID” turned on.
For example, say you first list all components that are panels, then you separate into groups based on type or  Clone  parameter. The first OP Find  DAT  pre-filters a huge hierarchy to a small fraction of the nodes, the subsequent OP Find DATs are operating on simpler sets to eliminate a lot of checking and cooking.
Refer to Help ->  Operator Snippets .
See also:  Script DAT

parameters.label: Active  Cook
parameters.name: activecook
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines when to cook the  DAT .

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: This stops the operator from cooking altogether.

parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.name: auto
parameters.description: Only cook / update the contents when the results would change.

parameters.label: Always
parameters.name: always
parameters.description: Continually cook this operator repeatedly for update cases that might be missed.

parameters.label: Incremental
parameters.name: incremental
parameters.description: This will cook each frame, but only add one result per cook, until all results are added. At that point cooking stops.

parameters.label: Cook   Pulse
parameters.name: cookpulse
parameters.description: Manually force the OP Find  DAT  to update.

parameters.label: Component
parameters.name: component
parameters.description: The path to the component where the search starts from.

parameters.label: Include  Component
parameters.name: includecomponent
parameters.description: Include the component the search starts from in the search itself.

parameters.label: Include  Wire   Hierarchy
parameters.name: includewired
parameters.description: Any components wired to the starting component are included in the search.

parameters.label: Minimum Depth
parameters.name: mindepth
parameters.description: Set a minmum depth for the sub-components the OP Find  DAT  should recursively search through.

parameters.label: Limit Max Depth
parameters.name: limitmaxdepth
parameters.description: Turns on the Maximum Depth parameter to limit searching through sub-components. Turning this toggle off will search through all sub-networks.

parameters.label: Maximum Depth
parameters.name: maxdepth
parameters.description: Set the maximum depth for the sub-components the OP Find  DAT  should recursively search through.

parameters.label: Limit Max Operators
parameters.name: limitmaxops
parameters.description: Limit the total number of operators iterated in the search.

parameters.label: Maximum Operators
parameters.name: maxops
parameters.description: Number of operators the search is limited to.

parameters.description: ⊞  - Combine 'All', 'Any' or 'Custom' of the filters below to get a match. 'Custom' allows for specifying a subselection of filters with 'or' and 'and' keywords.

parameters.label: All
parameters.name: all
parameters.description: All filters must match for an operator to be included in the search result. (AND)

parameters.label: Any
parameters.name: any
parameters.description: Any of the filter conditions must be met for an operator to be included in the search result. (OR)

parameters.label: Custom Combine

parameters.label: Name

parameters.description: Use the operator's names like 'wave1', 'wave2', etc.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.name: typefilter
parameters.description: Use names like  waveCHOP  and  panelexecuteDAT . Look at the column Type to see the syntax.

parameters.description: Specify a relative parent path that operators should be located in. This is a filter option on the  parentPath  column of this  DAT  that can be enabled by toggling the  Parent  Path   parameter on this  DAT 's  Columns  page.

parameters.label: Exclude  Path  (relative)

parameters.name: commentfilter
parameters.description: Only match operators that include the here specified comment string.

parameters.label: Tags
parameters.name: tagsfilter
parameters.description: Only match operators that match the here specified tags. Multiple tags can be searched for as a space seperated list.

parameters.label: DAT  Text

parameters.description: Only include operators that - in the case of being from the  DAT  family - match specified string in their content.

parameters.label: Par Name
